gym.label: Gym
gym.blurb: Machines at the gym. 5 sets of 5 reps. Add a little weight each time all 25 reps are clean.
gym.rest: Rest 2 to 3 minutes between sets. Take more if you need it.

learn.text: First 4 weeks: you may do 1 set of 8 with light dumbbells instead, to learn the hinge. After week 4, do 1 set of 5.

home.label: Home
home.blurb: Light dumbbells, bands or water jugs. 3 sets of 8 to 12 reps. Stop each set with 1 to 3 reps still in the tank. The last 2 reps should feel like work, not a grind.
home.rest: Rest 90 seconds to 2 minutes between sets (about 60 seconds for the deadlift and the extras).

v_squat.name: Hammer V-Squat
v_squat.author: coach
v_squat.setup: Feet in the middle of the platform, shoulder width. Shoulders under the pads. Back flat on the pad.
steps: Unlock the machine and stand tall.
Lower with control until your thighs are about parallel to the platform.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up.
Stop just short of locking your knees hard at the top.
v_squat.feel: Front of your thighs (quads) and your glutes.
mistakes: Feet too low on the platform
Locking your knees hard at the top
Lifting your hips off the pad
v_squat.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it.

alternatives.name: At home: Goblet Squat
alternatives.cue: Hold one weight at your chest and sit down between your hips.

v_squat.start_guess: Empty sled, or the bar plus about 10 lb per side.

iso_bench.name: Hammer Iso-Lateral Bench Press
iso_bench.step_note: If your gym has 2.5 lb plates, use them for presses. If not, add 5 lb per side instead.
iso_bench.author: coach
iso_bench.setup: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest. Pull your shoulder blades back and down against the pad.
steps: Grip the handles.
Press out until your arms are nearly straight.
Bring the handles back slowly, with control.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned back the whole time.
iso_bench.feel: Chest and the back of your arms (triceps).
iso_bench.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it.

alternatives.name: At home: Push-Up
alternatives.cue: Hands on a counter, body straight, chest to the counter.

iso_row.name: Hammer Iso-Lateral Row
iso_row.author: coach
iso_row.setup: Sit with your chest against the pad. Grab the handles with arms long.
steps: Pull your elbows back past your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are long again.
iso_row.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it.

alternatives.name: At home: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
alternatives.cue: One hand on a chair, pull your elbow to your hip.

iso_shoulder.name: Hammer Iso-Lateral Shoulder Press
iso_shoulder.step_note: If your gym has 2.5 lb plates, use them for presses. If not, add 5 lb per side instead.
iso_shoulder.author: coach
iso_shoulder.setup: Seat so the handles start about chin or ear level. Ribs down, glutes tight, back on the pad.
steps: Press straight up, not forward.
Stop just short of locking your elbows.
Lower back to chin or ear level with control.
iso_shoulder.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it.

db_sldl.name: Dumbbell Straight-Leg Deadlift
db_sldl.author: coach
db_sldl.setup: Feet hip width. Dumbbells in front of your thighs. Soft knees.
steps: Push your hips straight back, like closing a car door with your butt.
Let the dumbbells slide down your legs to mid-shin, or until you feel a good stretch in the back of your legs.
Keep your back flat the whole time.
Squeeze your glutes to stand back up.
db_sldl.feel: Back of your legs (hamstrings) and glutes.
mistakes: Dumbbells drifting forward away from your legs
Going so low your back rounds
db_sldl.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it. Your lower back should never hurt.

alternatives.name: Band good-morning or pull-through
alternatives.cue: Same hinge: band behind you or between your legs, hips back, flat back, squeeze glutes to stand.

goblet_squat.name: Goblet Squat
goblet_squat.author: coach
goblet_squat.setup: Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out. Hold the weight at your chest with elbows in. A dumbbell, a loaded backpack or a water jug all work.
steps: Sit down between your hips. Chest up.
Knees track over your toes.
Go as deep as you can with your heels flat.
Push the floor away to stand up.
goblet_squat.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it.

alternatives.name: Chair box squat (first 2 weeks)
alternatives.cue: If depth or balance feels shaky, sit back to a chair, touch lightly, stand up. Same cues. Put the chair against a wall so it can't slide. Touch lightly, don't plop down.

alternatives.name: Band squat
alternatives.cue: Stand on the band, hold the handles at your shoulders, elbows in. Squat with the same cues. Keep the band tight the whole time. Check the band for nicks or tears before each set. Anchor it on the hinge side of a closed door, or on a post, and stand clear of the snap path.

pushup.name: Push-Up
pushup.author: coach
pushup.setup: Hands just wider than your shoulders. Body in a straight line from head to knees or heels. Tighten your belly. Start with your hands on a counter or a sturdy table, that is the easiest.
steps: Lower your chest to the surface in about 2 seconds.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees, not flared out.
Press back up to straight arms.
Get stronger by lowering the surface: counter, then stairs, then knees, then the floor.
pushup.feel: Chest, front of shoulders, and triceps.
pushup.safety: Never push to failure on the floor. If the last reps get ugly, move up to a higher surface. Sharp or joint pain means skip and flag it.

alternatives.name: At the gym: Hammer Iso-Lateral Bench Press
alternatives.cue: Handles at mid chest, shoulder blades back.

pushup.start_guess: Pick a surface high enough that 12 reps feel easy. Start at the counter.

db_row.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
db_row.author: coach
db_row.setup: One hand on a chair or counter. Flat back. Weight in the other hand, arm long. Do your weaker side first, then match the reps on the other side. Log the reps from your weaker side.
steps: Pull your elbow toward your hip.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top for 1 second.
Lower slowly until your arm is long.
Switch sides: the other side gets the same reps and the same weight.
db_row.feel: Mid-back and lats (the sides of your back), not your neck.
db_row.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it.

alternatives.name: Band row
alternatives.cue: Use a door anchor at about chest height, or loop the band around a post. Stand tall, arms long, pull your elbows back to your sides, squeeze your shoulder blades for 1 second, return slowly. Check the band for nicks or tears before each set. Anchor it on the hinge side of a closed door, or on a post, and stand clear of the snap path.

db_ohp.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
db_ohp.author: coach
db_ohp.setup: Seated or standing. Ribs down, glutes tight. Dumbbells at chin or ear level.
steps: Press straight overhead, slightly in front of your ears, not behind.
Lower back to chin or ear level with control.
db_ohp.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it.

alternatives.name: Band press
alternatives.cue: Stand on the band, handles at your shoulders. Ribs down, glutes tight, press straight up, lower slowly. Check the band for nicks or tears before each set. Anchor it on the hinge side of a closed door, or on a post, and stand clear of the snap path.

db_rdl.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
db_rdl.author: coach
db_rdl.setup: Feet hip width. Dumbbells in front of your thighs. Soft knees.
steps: Push your hips straight back, like closing a car door with your butt.
Let the dumbbells slide down your legs to mid-shin, or until you feel a good stretch in the back of your legs.
Keep your back flat the whole time.
Squeeze your glutes to stand back up.
db_rdl.feel: Back of your legs (hamstrings) and glutes.
mistakes: Going so low your back rounds
db_rdl.safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip this one today and flag it. Your lower back should never hurt.

alternatives.name: Band good-morning or pull-through
alternatives.cue: Same hinge cue with the band behind you or between your legs.

band_pull_apart.name: Band Pull-Apart (optional)
band_pull_apart.author: donald
band_pull_apart.setup: Stand tall. Hold a light band in front of your chest, arms straight, hands shoulder width.
steps: Pull the band apart by moving your hands out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end for 1 second.
Return slowly.
band_pull_apart.feel: Upper back and the back of your shoulders. Good for posture.
band_pull_apart.safety: Use a light band. Check the band for nicks or tears before each set. Anchor it on the hinge side of a closed door, or on a post, and stand clear of the snap path. Sharp or joint pain means skip and flag it.
band_pull_apart.start_guess: Lightest band. Log weight as 0 or the band color number.

glute_bridge.name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge (optional)
glute_bridge.author: donald
glute_bridge.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip width. Rest a dumbbell across your hips and hold it.
steps: Ribs down: tighten your belly so your lower back stays flat.
Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes at the top for 1 second. Keep your ribs down, do not arch.
Lower slowly.
glute_bridge.feel: Glutes. A little in the back of your legs.
mistakes: Arching your lower back at the top
glute_bridge.safety: Pad the weight with a towel. Sharp or joint pain means skip and flag it.

alternatives.name: No weight
alternatives.cue: Do it with body weight only, same cues.

glute_bridge.start_guess: Body weight first, then 10 to 15 lb.

warmup.title: 5-minute warm-up
steps: March in place, 1 minute.
Arm circles, forward and back, 1 minute.
Bodyweight squats, slow, 10 to 15 reps.
One light set of your first exercise. Tap Warm-up when you log it.

start_guide.title: Find your start weight
start_guide.text: Your first session is a technique session. Pick a weight you can do 12 clean reps with and could do 4 more. That is your start weight. Do not test your max.
notes: First 2 weeks: go lighter than you think. Good form matters more than speed.
Expect some soreness after week 1. That is normal and it fades.
Week 1: if every rep feels easy, add a little weight next time.

schedule: 3 days a week, never 2 days in a row (for example Mon, Wed, Fri). Alternate A, B, A, then B, A, B the next week. 2 days a week is fine when life is busy.
safety: Sharp pain, pain in a joint, or pain that lasts for days means skip that exercise and flag it. Stop any time something hurts sharply.
